# Effort management

Binary-owned effort records and optional resources.

**Applicability:** Owning domain selectors: `cmd/**`, `internal/audit/**`, `internal/authoringop/**`, `internal/changelog/**`, `internal/checkop/**`, `internal/clispec/**`, `internal/commitmsg/**`, `internal/commitpolicy/**`, `internal/configop/**`, `internal/currentstatecoord/**`, `internal/domainop/**`, `internal/effort/**`, `internal/evals/**`, `internal/filepublication/**`, `internal/filesystem/**`, `internal/git/**`, `internal/initop/**`, `internal/initspec/**`, `internal/localdocop/**`, `internal/memorycite/**`, `internal/pitfallop/**`, `internal/projectlicense/**`, `internal/prosegate/**`, `internal/repositorycheck/**`, `internal/severity/**`, `internal/snapshot/**`, `internal/testselection/**`, `internal/testsupport/**`, `internal/topicop/**`, `internal/upgrade/**`, `internal/worktree/**`, `test-selection.json`, `tools/**`, `x`. Topic selectors: `cmd/awf/effort*.go`, `internal/effort/**`, `internal/worktree/**`. Both domain and topic selectors must match. Run `awf read topic tooling/effort-management --coverage` for current applicable and owned paths and marker sites.

The awf binary owns lightweight repository-local effort records and their optional resident resources. These records coordinate local work without replacing tracked project authority.

## Claims

### `invariant: effort-record-authority`

The awf binary accepts a caller-supplied canonical slug through 32 bytes when minting a new immutable slug/UUID identity, retains canonical resident reads and command selection through 63 bytes, and owns schema-2 `state.json`, required safely owned `memory.md`, optional ignored `activity.json`, and one optional owned real `scratch/` directory under `.awf/efforts/<slug>/`. Resident creation publishes the fixed memory skeleton before identity state; an ordinary retry resumes only an empty or exact skeleton-only slug directory and refuses every other pre-existing shape. `state.json` alone owns effort identity. Memory and activity bytes are opaque to awf after memory creation: lifecycle code does not parse legacy memory frontmatter or create, read, parse, validate, mutate, or independently delete activity. Scratch descendants are likewise opaque. Directory presence remains the active-effort fact; listing and selection preserve and refuse foreign direct resident entries and do not inspect `.awf/effort-archive` descendants. Missing or unsafe required memory, invalid state, unsafe ownership, and foreign direct leaves refuse lifecycle mutation. After managed topology, resident safety, the exact archive root, the fully rendered self-ignore marker, and destination absence are validated, finish atomically moves the complete unchanged active directory without replacement to `.awf/effort-archive/<uuid>-<slug>` in one step. The move archives accepted memory, activity, and scratch bytes unchanged and releases the slug; pre-move failure leaves the active resident available for inspection and ordinary retry, while collisions and cross-device moves refuse without copy/delete. The archive is ignored, unmanaged, non-authoritative, invisible to effort inventory, and manually disposable; awf provides no archive inventory, restore, prune, analysis, retention, force-delete, or bypass surface.
Backing: test

### `invariant: managed-worktree-lifecycle`

The six effort commands cross one `internal/effort/application` boundary, which owns lifecycle and managed-worktree coordination, mutation-lease selection, and presentation mapping. Resident storage and safety remain in `internal/effort`; managed Git-topology mechanics remain in `internal/worktree`. Managed effort worktrees are stateless native-Git utilities at `.awf/worktrees/<slug>/` on `awf/<slug>`. Integration revalidates a clean target, exact registration, repository identity, branch, operation state, and ancestry immediately before mutation; it reports already-contained history, fast-forwards, or starts a divergent `--no-commit` merge, never tests, reviews, commits, pushes, resolves, removes, records disposition, or finishes. Remove independently inspects path, exact registration, branch, and target ancestry on every retry. Native Git refuses tracked and nonignored untracked work, while an explicit ignored-path probe prevents Git from silently deleting ignored data. Unrelated target-checkout changes do not block removal, an unregistered managed path is preserved for manual inspection, and awf exposes no force-discard path.
Backing: test

### `invariant: default-worktree-creation`

`awf effort new --slug <slug> <outcome-title>` feeds the required explicit slug through resident publication, then creates the managed worktree through the same standalone Add machinery at `.awf/worktrees/<slug>/` on `awf/<slug>`, based on the invoking checkout's `HEAD` unless `--base <ref>` selects another base. If Add fails, the new resident remains visible and the failure names the managed path and branch for inspection before an ordinary `awf effort worktree add <slug>` retry. No failed-creation rollback, finishing reservation, inferred topology state, or resident deletion occurs. Success reports the worktree path and branch and directs continuation there.
Backing: test

### `invariant: memory-skeleton-purpose-partition`

New memory is plain Markdown with `## Brief`, `## Checkpoint`, `## Decision log`, `## Observations`, and `## Handoff log`, with each placeholder naming its contract and consumer. It contains no machine frontmatter. The workflow, not the binary, defines section use and the one-writer update protocol. Existing memory bytes, including old four-key YAML frontmatter and arbitrary old `phase`, `next`, or `updated` values, remain accepted and are never rewritten merely because their format is legacy. Awf exposes no special memory read, edit, update, metadata, owner, preview, diff, clock, or presentation protocol.
Backing: test

### `rule: managed-effort-format-support`

Schema-2 state, required safely owned opaque Markdown memory, optional ignored opaque activity bytes, managed worktree topology, and byte-preserving archive moves remain current lifecycle formats.
